item.title: Fed’s Christopher Waller opens door to 50-basis-point December rate hike after hot CPI
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point December rate hike after US core inflation rose 0.3% in October. Persistent price pressures have intensified debate over tighter monetary policy and the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's remarks intensified the debate over a possible half-percentage-point interest-rate increase in December after US inflation data came in hotter than expected on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.In a speech delivered in London before the release of October’s Consumer Price Index, Waller said he was inclined to support a rate increase in December. He warned that a 50-basis-point move might be necessary if inflation continued to accelerate, arguing that the Fed’s credibility could otherwise be at risk.Hours later, data showed that consumer prices rose more than expected. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% from the previous month, meeting the threshold Waller identified as grounds for considering a larger rate increase.Also read: Traders raise odds of 50 bps Fed rate hike as CPI rise exceeds expectationsWaller’s remarks represent the clearest signal yet from a Fed official that policymakers may need to raise rates in December by more than the quarter-percentage-point move markets had expected.Several senior Fed officials, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams, are scheduled to speak this week.Fed watchers said Waller’s comments did not make a 50-basis-point move certain but would add urgency to the debate over how aggressively policymakers must act to contain inflation.“This is not a print that screams out the need to go 50, but certainly provides ammunition to the argument to do so,” Christopher Hodge, chief US economist at Natixis, told Bloomberg.For live updates on US Markets, click hereTom Porcelli, chief economist at Wells Fargo, said he expected the Fed’s policy-setting committee to support another rate increase unanimously, although the size of the move remained open for debate.“This locks it down,” Porcelli said, referring to the likelihood of at least a 25-basis-point increase. “With Waller introducing that idea, the market is going to run with it in the face of this firm print.”Following Waller’s remarks and the inflation report, investors priced in a more aggressive path for interest rates in the coming months. However, markets remained unconvinced that policymakers would deliver a half-point increase in December.Federal funds futures continued to indicate a quarter-point move in December, followed by additional increases of the same size in January and possibly April. Investors had previously expected rate increases in December and March.Waller described the US economy as strong and the labour market as stable but said inflation remained too high.“If, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points,” Waller said.“But if the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3% or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed,” he added. “In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.”Under such a scenario, Waller said a conventional quarter-point increase would do little to reassure the public that the Fed was serious about controlling inflation.“Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take,” he said.Also Read: Are days of easy money over? Aswath Damodaran warns of a new mkt realityHot CPI intensifies rate debateData released later by the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October from the previous month, while the headline CPI increased 0.4%.Fed officials held interest rates steady last month, saying the “accumulation of more information” would help them determine the appropriate policy setting.The 10-2 decision followed a unanimous vote in September to raise the benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4%. Several policymakers have since indicated that additional increases may be necessary.Data released last week showed that job growth accelerated in October while the unemployment rate edged lower. Fed officials will receive another employment report and a full set of inflation data before their December meeting.During a question-and-answer session with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua after the speech, Waller said the Fed did not want to “slam the economy down.”“It’s not that we’re going to jack up the policy rate 150 basis points or 200 basis points,” he said. “We are looking forward and saying we need to do something; at a minimum, probably take back the three insurance cuts that we put in last year.”Waller added that monetary policy had not been “nearly as restrictive as I thought it was.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Anthropic's potential mega IPO joins ranks of world's biggest stock market listings
item.description: Anthropic has kicked off its U.S. IPO roadshow, seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion by offering 825 million shares. This latest valuation stands at roughly $1.4 trillion, representing a drop from earlier estimations of $2 trillion. Notably, tech giants like Alphabet and Microsoft are set to invest $26 billion in a private placement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its hotly anticipated US initial public offering on Tuesday, bringing the Claude maker a step closer to a landmark debut that is set to test investor appetite for the rapidly growing AI industry.The listing would represent what is expected to be one of the largest debuts ever attempted, potentially reshaping benchmark indexes, investor flows and the broader narrative driving US equities.A GLANCE AT WORLD'S BIGGEST IPOsThe biggest IPOs globally, ranked by deal size:ANTHROPICThe filing confirmed Reuters reporting that Anthropic and some existing shareholders were seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion in its U.S. IPO, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each and targeting a valuation of about $1.4 trillion.Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, but expectations have since fallen amid Anthropic's hefty infrastructure commitments and volatility in AI-related stocks. Reuters previously reported that about $1.5 trillion was viewed as the high end of the range.Anthropic has also lined up $26 billion from some of the world's biggest technology companies in a private placement alongside the IPO, highlighting the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC have agreed to participate in the private placement at the IPO price.Details of the blockbuster offering were briefly circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.The IPO has already been pushed back from earlier plans, with Reuters previously reporting that marketing was expected to begin in mid-October at the earliest.Reuters has previously reported details of Anthropic's financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans.Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers who left OpenAI after disagreements over governance and AI safety,raised $65 billion at a post-money valuation of $965 billion in late May.OPENAIOpenAI, which operates AI chatbot ChatGPT, revealed in June that it had confidentially filed for a US IPO.The company will not go public in 2026, CEO Sam Altman had said in September, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence that render unacceptable even a 10% risk that AI could cause human extinction by decade's end.OpenAI President Greg Brockman last week said the company now generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he believes it will be ready to go public in 2027.The company has been racing to ramp up fundraising, Reuters has reported, in order to capitalize on its recent growth after delaying its IPO plans.OpenAI has closed on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, Reuters reported last week.In May, OpenAI fended off an existential court challenge from Elon Musk, simplifying the path for it to proceed with a stock market listing. We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company. But it's a complicated set of tradeoffs and this gives us the option to go public sooner if that ends up being best, OpenAI had said in June.SPACEXElon Musk's rocket and satellite maker SpaceX made a historic Nasdaq debut in June, raising a record $75 billion and eclipsing Saudi Aramco's 2019 listing to become the world's largest IPO.The offering broke with Wall Street convention by setting the price before the investor roadshow, which is typically used to gauge demand and establish a price range. Its proceeds were more than double those of Saudi Aramco;s IPO.SpaceX shares ended their first trading day at $160.95, valuing the company at $2.1 trillion. The stock has since lost momentum, closing at $142.07 on November 9, but remained above its $135 IPO price.

item.title: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO, targets up to $90.4 billion in fundraising
item.description: Anthropic is targeting a fully diluted $1.4 trillion valuation through its proposed IPO, seeking up to $64.35 billion. Combined with a $26 billion private placement, fundraising could reach $90.4 billion amid rising infrastructure costs and competition.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Gaurav
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is targeting a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its proposed initial public offering (IPO), setting the stage for one of the largest stock market listings as the artificial intelligence company prepares to tap public investors. The Claude maker has launched its IPO roadshow, offering 825 million shares in a price band of $70-78 apiece. The company is seeking to raise up to $64.35 billion through the public offering, according to its regulatory filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).The proposed issue comprises 801.35 million shares being issued by Anthropic and another 23.65 million shares offered by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the price band, the company could generate gross proceeds of approximately $62.51 billion from its primary share sale, before expenses, according to reports.Anthropic is also looking to raise an additional $26 billion through a separate private placement involving cornerstone investors, including Alphabet's Google, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). Combined, the IPO and private placement could take the total fundraising to as much as $90.4 billion.The targeted $1.4 trillion valuation is calculated on a fully diluted basis, factoring in securities such as stock options and restricted shares. At the top end of the IPO price range, Anthropic's market capitalisation would be approximately $1 trillion on a non-diluted basis, Reuters reported.The valuation target, however, is lower than the $2 trillion figure that some investors had previously discussed. Expectations have moderated amid the company's sizeable infrastructure commitments and volatility in AI-related stocks.ALSO READ: Anthropic's IPO: A close look at AI frontrunner's rapid growth, spiraling costsAI ambitions meet mounting infrastructure costsAnthropic's proposed listing comes at a time when investors are increasingly scrutinising the economics of artificial intelligence, particularly the enormous computing investments required to develop, train and operate advanced AI models.The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Alphabet's Google. These commitments highlight the scale of resources required to sustain its expansion and the importance of securing future computing capacity.Despite the substantial infrastructure requirements, Anthropic has reported rapid revenue growth, supported by increasing demand for its Claude family of AI models.According to its IPO filing, the company's run-rate revenue stood at approximately $81 billion as of October 31, up from the previous month. Revenue increased 47% sequentially to $16.96 billion in the third quarter, although the pace of growth moderated from the 144% increase recorded in the preceding quarter.Anthropic attributed the expansion to growing adoption of Claude, including specialised products designed for industries such as healthcare, financial services and legal services.However, the company remains loss-making, reflecting the significant expenditure involved in developing and scaling artificial intelligence systems.IPO document highlights competition, AI safety risksAnthropic's regulatory filing has also laid out several risks that could affect its business, ranging from intensifying competition to the challenges of ensuring the safe deployment of increasingly capable AI systems.The company warned that competitors could gain an advantage by developing AI models at a faster pace. It also flagged the risk that advances in artificial intelligence could outstrip its ability to implement adequate safety and security measures.Regulatory hurdles and increased government oversight could pose further challenges, particularly as Anthropic expands the infrastructure required to support its operations.The disclosures come amid growing concerns about AI agents operating beyond their intended environments and the potential misuse of increasingly sophisticated AI tools to breach protected networks.IPO could set new fundraising benchmarkAnthropic's proposed offering could rank among the largest IPOs in market history, following SpaceX's $75 billion stock market debut in June at a valuation of nearly $1.75 trillion. The figure excludes additional shares purchased by underwriters through the greenshoe option.The proposed listing has attracted interest from several major technology companies and investors. Apart from Google, Nvidia and AMD, broader investment commitments include companies such as Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC).Certain members of Anthropic's board and entities affiliated with them have also expressed interest in purchasing up to $303 million worth of shares in the offering.Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT.The offering will be made through a prospectus, with preliminary copies available through Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, among the underwriters managing the transaction.The registration statement covering the securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet become effective.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser.
